claims.claim: The web app renders a static foundation landing shell with semantic landmarks, a skip link, and explicit status disclosures.
A shared token package defines the initial ocean, sky, white, sand, and seafoam palette.
The API exposes a fixed, non-leaking liveness response.
The API checks real database connectivity and truthfully reports HTTP 200/ready when reachable or HTTP 503/not-ready when it is not.
Every API error response uses a typed envelope with a stable error code and a request ID, and every response carries a matching X-Request-ID header.
Passwords are hashed with bcrypt, never logged or returned, and login issues an expiring, revocable session token that is rejected once expired or revoked.

Server-side role checks and organization-scoped queries prevent a member of one organization from reading or acting on another organization's data, returning a not-found response instead of leaking existence.
Login and the admin-only demonstration endpoint each append an immutable audit event; audit rows reject in-place updates and deletes at the database level.
The seed script creates the same synthetic organizations, memberships, and demo accounts every time it runs against an empty database, with no real personal data.
A typed TypeScript client package covers every implemented API endpoint (health, login, /me, org members) with response types mirrored from the API schemas.

The web app renders Home, Initiatives, Projects, and Evidence pages behind one accessible shared shell with a skip link and current-page navigation, and reuses shared status and case-study card primitives.

Harbor deterministically compares synthetic need category, controlled eligibility, coarse zone, open status, capacity freshness and availability, and accessibility while returning score components, rejections, and uncertainty; protected traits are absent.
Harbor reserves current capacity only after explicit coordinator approval using an atomic conditional update and a database no-overbooking constraint, including a concurrent SQLite test.

Harbor enforces organization scope and role boundaries server-side: visitors see safe demo records, coordinators and admins change workflow state, and volunteers receive assignment-only synthetic fields.
The Harbor route presents impact and engineering evidence plus a keyboard-operable request-to-audit synthetic workflow with semantic loading, empty, and error states using the typed API client.
The web app publishes an accessible Haven page that keeps diagnosis out, surfaces emergency 911/988 guidance, and demonstrates synthetic navigation with curated resources and reviewable plans.
The shared design tokens now carry a navy accent while preserving the cloud-bright Zion palette and sky-based theme.
The homepage surfaces the Harbor and Haven flagship project pages with direct links and keeps the cloud-bright, navy-accented direction explicit.
The projects index surfaces the Harbor and Haven project routes first and keeps the supporting foundation cards separate.
The Community Aid Hub page presents purpose, audience, features, limitations, and evidence for the synthetic community-aid coordination route.
The Health Navigator page presents purpose, audience, features, limitations, and evidence for the synthetic health-access route.
